item.title: Promising new biomarkers to diagnose feline chronic kidney disease
item.description: [Diabetes & Kidney Disease] Keyword: kidney disease — Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is common in cats but often goes undiagnosed until it's at a late stage. Thanks to a recent study published in the Journal of Proteome Research, researchers have new leads to determine how feline CKD develops. The paper reports collections of potential protein biomarkers in urine that could help veterinarians detect different stages of the disease and develop more targeted and effective treatments for this irreversible ailment.

item.title: Scientists discover stunning new Amazon fish that may already be endangered
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: deforestation — Researchers have discovered a stunning new species of tiny orange-patterned fish in the Brazilian Amazon, but its survival may already be at risk. Named Laimosemion laranja, the brilliantly colored killifish measures less than three centimeters long and was found in just three small forest pools. Its extremely limited habitat is threatened by mining, deforestation, pollution, and expanding development.

item.title: An ancient ocean full of giant predators reveals a surprising twist in evolution
item.description: [Open Source Software] Keyword: FOSS — A remarkable fossil discovery in Colombia is challenging how scientists understand major evolutionary changes in Earth's history. Researchers uncovered an incredibly diverse ancient marine ecosystem where giant reptiles, sharks, and other creatures thrived as older evolutionary groups approached extinction and newer ones emerged. They call this previously unrecognized pattern a "Biotic Inflection," suggesting that major transformations in life can occur without mass extinctions.

item.title: A little-known protein could be a major culprit in type 2 diabetes
item.description: [Diabetes & Kidney Disease] Keyword: type 2 diabetes — Scientists have discovered that a buildup of a protein called Miro1 may be a hidden driver of insulin resistance in Type 2 diabetes, with preclinical experiments showing that removing it restores the muscles’ response to insulin. Exercise was also found to lower Miro1 levels in people with diabetes, revealing a potential new pathway for treating the disease.
